Convert a community matrix to long format

Source: R/community.R
community_to_long.Rd

Turns a community matrix (one row per sample, one column per species, as used by vegan and most community-ecology software) and a table describing the samples into the long format used by check_coverage(), fit_isodars() and niche_breadth(): one row per species x site x habitat.

Usage

community_to_long(comm, samples, site, habitat, effort = NULL, keep = NULL)

Arguments

comm

A matrix or data frame of counts: one row per sample, one column per species (column names are the species names). Counts must be non-negative and not missing.

samples

A data frame with one row per row of comm, in the same order, giving the site, habitat and (optionally) effort of each sample.

site, habitat

Names of the site and habitat columns of samples.

effort

Optional name of the effort column of samples (area, transect length, trap nights...; positive).

keep

Optional names of other site-level columns of samples to carry over, such as longitude and latitude for group_sites(). They must have one value per site.

Value

A tibble with columns species, the site and habitat columns (named as in samples), abundance, effort (named as in samples, or "effort" = number of samples) and any keep columns, ready for niche_breadth(x, species = "species", site = ..., habitat = ..., abundance = "abundance", effort = ...). Pass the effort column as effort: without it, every pooled site x habitat counts as equal effort (fit_isodars() and niche_breadth() warn when it is left out).

Details

Each row of comm is one sample (a transect, quadrat, trap, count...) and the matching row of samples says at which site and in which habitat it was taken. Samples taken at the same site and habitat are pooled: counts are summed, and so are efforts. Without an effort column, every sample has effort 1, so the effort of a site x habitat is its number of samples; sites and habitats sampled unevenly are then still compared as densities per sample.

Every sampled site x habitat appears for every species, with 0 where the species was not recorded (which is what makes zeros informative). Species never recorded are dropped.

See also

check_coverage(), niche_breadth(), vignette("data-preparation")

Examples

comm <- matrix(c(5, 0, 2,
                 3, 1, 0,
                 0, 4, 6,
                 1, 2, 2), nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE,
               dimnames = list(NULL, c("sp_a", "sp_b", "sp_c")))
samples <- data.frame(site = c("s1", "s1", "s1", "s2"),
                      habitat = c("reef", "reef", "lagoon", "reef"))
community_to_long(comm, samples, site = "site", habitat = "habitat")
#> # A tibble: 9 × 5
#>   species site  habitat abundance effort
#>   <chr>   <chr> <chr>       <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 sp_a    s1    lagoon          0      1
#> 2 sp_a    s1    reef            8      2
#> 3 sp_a    s2    reef            1      1
#> 4 sp_b    s1    lagoon          4      1
#> 5 sp_b    s1    reef            1      2
#> 6 sp_b    s2    reef            2      1
#> 7 sp_c    s1    lagoon          6      1
#> 8 sp_c    s1    reef            2      2
#> 9 sp_c    s2    reef            2      1
